reference/reference.text: Reference go-ui has two packages: Package Import What it is ui ui "github.com/akrck02/go-ui" The context, layout, every control, themes, screen readers window "github.com/akrck02/go-ui/window" A window that runs an interface: on the desktop, in a web page, on Android; preferences, notifications, films ui.md and window.md list every type and function with the first sentence of its comment; they are generated from the doc comments ( python3 docs/6-reference/generate.py ). go doc github.com/akrck02/go-ui.Context.Table prints any of them whole. This page is the map: the context's methods by what they are for. The frame Method ui.New() (*Context, error) A context that measures text with go-renderer's fonts; NewWithMeasurer takes another (tests) Begin(state *input.State) , End() Open and close a frame: End lays out, paints and claims the mouse and keyboard. window.Run calls both for you Drawing() *draw2d.List What go-renderer paints: give it to scene.Overlay.Drawing once Push(name) , Pop() Open and close a scope, so controls in a loop have ids of their own Area(path...) (draw2d.Rect, bool) Where a control was drawn in the last frame, by its scopes and label RequestFrame(delay) Ask for another frame within a delay, for something that moves Size() (width, height) , Insets() The window's size, and how much of each edge the system's bars cover Theme (field) The tokens every control reads: ui.LightTheme() , ui.DarkTheme() Layout Method Box(layout, content) Arranges its children Frame(layout, look, content) Arranges and paints: fill, border, radius, shadow, clip Row(content) , Column(content) , Grid(columns, content) Shortcuts with the theme's gap Spacer() , Separator() Free space; a thin line ScrollArea(name, layout, content) Content that scrolls; ScrollOffset(name) , ScrollPull(name) Resizable(name, side, &size, minimum, maximum, layout, content) A box with an edge to drag Fold(name, open, duration, layout, content) A box that opens to its content's height and closes, with motion SwipeBox(name, layout, axis, content) A box a finger swipes sideways: pages, cards Sizes: ui.Fit() , ui.Grow() , ui.GrowBy(weight) , ui.Share(weight) , ui.Fixed(pixels) , ui.Percent(share) , each .Between(minimum, maximum) . Padding: ui.Pad(all) , ui.PadXY(horizontal, vertical) . Alignment: ui.Start , ui.Center , ui.End . Text and pictures Method Heading(text) , Label(text) , Caption(text) A title, body text, a quiet hint Text(text, ui.TextStyle{Size, Weight, Color}) Any size, weight and colour Icon(name) , IconSized(name, size, colour) A Lucide icon Image(picture, layout, radius) A draw2d.Image , cropped to fill its box Paint(layout, paint func(area, drawing)) A box you paint yourself, once laid out SetTextScale(scale) , TextScale() Every text larger or smaller (the system's font size) Controls Method Returns true when Button(label) , PrimaryButton(label) Clicked IconButton(icon, label) , PrimaryIconButton(icon, label) Clicked; square with an empty label FlatButton(label) , FlatIconButton(icon, label) Clicked; no fill until hovered (toolbars) Selectable(icon, label, selected) Clicked Clickable(name, layout, looks, content) Clicked: any box, with a look per state Checkbox(label, &value) , Toggle(label, &value) Changed Slider(name, &value, minimum, maximum) , SliderStep(…, step) Changed NumberField(name, &value, minimum, maximum, step, format) Changed TextField(name, &text) , TextFieldWith(name, &text, ui.TextFieldOptions{…}) Changed Select(name, &selected, options) Changed Tabs(name, &selected, labels...) Changed ListBox(name, layout, items, &selected) Changed Chip(icon, label, ui.ChipLook{…}) Clicked; RemovableChip returns clicked, removed MenuButton(icon, label, content) with MenuItem(icon, label, hint) MenuItem : chosen Tooltip(text) Explains the control before it LongPressed() The control before it was held, or right-clicked Text fields also have FieldFocused(name) , FocusField(name) , Focus(path...) , Typing() , the clipboard ( Copy(text) , ClipboardText() ), and for on-screen keyboards TypedField() and EditTypedField(edit) ; the bar over a selection is worded by SetEditingWords . Lists and tables Method List(name, layout, count, rowHeight, row func(index)) Equal rows, only those in sight built Table(name, layout, columns, rows func(*ui.Table)) A header and rows; table.Group(caption) , table.Row(key, selected, cells...) returns true when clicked Layers Method PanelWith(title, ui.PanelOptions{…}, content) , Panel(title, content) A floating card with a title bar, or docked to an edge Sheet(title, ui.SheetOptions{Width}, content) (dismissed bool) A modal card Modal(name, ui.LayerOptions{…}, content) (dismissed bool) Your content over everything, dimming the rest Overlay(name, ui.LayerOptions{…}, content) Your content over everything, without dimming Popover(name, &open, look, content) A box under the control before it Toast(text, warning) A short note at the bottom, fired once Pointer, touch and keyboard Method WantsMouse() , WantsKeyboard() Whether the interface claimed them in the last frame KeyboardNavigation ( WhenGiven , Always ), TakeKeyboard() , ReleaseKeyboard() , HasKeyboard() When Tab, Enter and Space move between controls and press them, and when they stay with a game or a 3D view ( who has the keyboard ) LessMotion Held controls keep their size, for people who asked the system for less motion Pointer() (x, y) , Pressing() Where the pointer is; whether it is held Touches() The fingers on a touch screen Back() Answers the system's back (a phone's gesture); sheets and modals answer first DragSource(name, payload, layout, content) , DropTarget(name, layout, accepts, content) Drag a value of yours from a box to another Dragging() , DroppedOnScreen() A drag in progress; a drop on the open screen (the scene) Motion Method Animate(name, target, duration) float32 Eases a value to its target, asking for frames while it moves Appear(name, duration) float32 Eases from 0 to 1 the first time something is shown LayerOptions.Leave A modal or overlay leaves with motion Screen readers Method Describe(ui.Description{Role, Label, Value, Checked, …}) What the control before it is, for a screen reader SetScreenReader(on) , ScreenReaderOn() , ScreenReaderNodes() The list of what can be read, made each frame while one is on ScreenReaderAct(id, action) , ScreenReaderSetText(id, text) , SetScreenReaderFocus(id) What the screen reader asks, done in the next frame The window does all of this on Android; see the guide . The window Function window.Run(options, build) Opens the window and calls build every frame window.RunWith(context, options, build) The same with a context you made (to set a theme or a measurer first) window.Options{…} Title , Width , Height , MinWidth , MinHeight , Dark , Continuous , Backend , Canvas , Scene , MaxFramesPerSecond , Hidden , Shown , CapturePath ; RegisterFlags(flags) window.Wake() A frame, from another goroutine window.KeepPreference , Preference , ForgetPreference Settings kept between runs window.SystemPrefersDark() , SystemPalettes() The system's theme and, on Android 12+, the wallpaper's colours window.Notify , AskForNotifications , NotificationsAllowed Notifications on a phone window.OpenLink(link) , Share(title, text) , FeelLongPress() The system's browser, its share sheet, a buzz window.OpenVideo(film) A film the phone or the browser decodes window.Graphics() , LastCrash() What draws; the last crash's report, on a phone ← Documentation

reference/ui.title: go-ui
reference/ui.text: go-ui import "github.com/akrck02/go-ui" Package ui builds interfaces (panels, buttons, labels…) over a go-renderer view, in immediate mode: every frame the program describes the interface again from its own variables, and each control answers what happened to it (a button returns true on the frame it is clicked). Nothing has to be kept in step with the program's data, because the interface holds none of it. A frame goes: ui.Begin(state) // the frame's mouse and keyboard ui.Panel("Light", func() { // controls, nested in boxes if ui.Button("Switch on") { light.On = true } }) ui.End() // lay out, paint, claim the mouse if it is over the interface and world.Overlay.Drawing = ui.Drawing() makes go-renderer paint it over the scene. Layout is deferred: controls are boxes in a tree that is sized and placed in End, with rules like a flexible box (fit the content, grow into free space, fixed or a percentage, padding, gaps, alignment). Controls react to the mouse using where they were drawn in the previous frame, a frame earlier than they are drawn now: invisible at sixty frames a second, and it lets a box be sized by things declared after it. Constants and variables var EnglishEditingWords = EditingWords{Cut: "Cut", Copy: "Copy", Paste: "Paste", SelectAll: "Select all"} EnglishEditingWords are the bar's labels unless a program sets others (SetEditingWords). AccessibleNode AccessibleNode is one thing a screen reader can read and act on. type AccessibleNode struct { ID ID // the same from one frame to the next while the thing stays Parent ID // the scroll area it is in, or 0 for the window Area draw2d.Rect // where it shows, in layout pixels: the part a scroll area does not hide Description Pressable bool // a double tap presses it (ReaderPress) LongPressable bool // the program reads LongPressed after it (ReaderLongPress) Scrollable bool // ReaderForward and ReaderBackward scroll it, or move a slider Typing bool // the keyboard types in it now } Align Align places children inside the free space of their box, along one axis. type Align int const ( Start Align = iota // left or top Center // in the middle End // right or bottom ) ChipLook ChipLook is a chip's own colours: its fill and the ink of its text and icon. The zero value uses the theme's quiet colours (Sunken and InkSoft). type ChipLook struct { Fill, Ink draw2d.Color } Column Column is one column of a table: its title, its width and where its cells sit. type Column struct { Title string // Width is the column's width. Use Fixed for narrow columns and Share for the rest: shares // start from nothing, so the header and every row come out the same. Width Sizing Align Align // Start for words, End for numbers // Weight is the face of its cells: draw2d.Mono for a column of codes. Weight draw2d.Weight } Context Context holds an interface between frames: what was where, what the mouse is on, which panel is in front, and the small state controls keep (a panel's position). Use one per window, from the goroutine that runs the update steps. type Context struct { Theme Theme // KeyboardNavigation says when the interface reads Tab, Enter and Space (focus.go). KeyboardNavigation KeyboardNavigation // LessMotion keeps controls still when the person asks the system for less motion: a held // control does not shrink. The program sets it from the platform's setting. LessMotion bool // Has unexported fields. } Function or method func New() (*Context, error) New returns an interface that measures text with go-renderer's fonts, in the default theme. func NewWithMeasurer(measurer draw2d.Measurer) *Context NewWithMeasurer returns an interface that measures text with a measurer of your choice: tests use a fake one, so they need no fonts. func (ui *Context) Animate(name string, target float32, duration time.Duration) float32 Animate eases a value towards a target over a duration, starting again from where it is when the target changes: a switch's handle going across, a tab's underline moving to the tab chosen. func (ui *Context) Appear(name string, duration time.Duration) float32 Appear goes from 0 to 1 over a duration from the frame something was first shown after it was not: a dialog fading and rising in, a note sliding up. func (ui *Context) Area(path ...string) (draw2d.Rect, bool) Area tells where a control was drawn in the last frame, found by its label and the scopes around it, outermost first: Area("Properties", "Apply") is the Apply button of the Properties panel (panels open a scope with their title). func (ui *Context) Back() bool Back answers the system's back (a phone's back gesture or button) in this frame, and tells whether there was one: the part of the interface the person is in goes back (a screen returns to the one before) and returns true. func (ui *Context) Begin(state *input.State) Begin starts describing the interface for a frame, with the frame's input. func (ui *Context) Box(layout Layout, content func()) Box adds a box with a layout, and what content adds goes inside it. func (ui *Context) Button(label string) bool Button adds a button and returns true on the frame it is clicked (pressed and let go over it). func (ui *Context) Caption(text string) Caption adds a line of small, quiet text: a hint or a unit. func (ui *Context) Checkbox(label string, value *bool) bool Checkbox adds a box to tick with a label after it; clicking either flips value. func (ui *Context) Chip(icon, label string, look ChipLook) bool Chip adds a small rounded label with an optional icon (a Lucide name), in its own colours: a tag, a state, a filter. func (ui *Context) Clickable(name string, layout Layout, looks Looks, content func()) bool Clickable adds a box that reacts to the mouse, with whatever content, and returns true on the step it is clicked: the building block for controls of your own (a table row, a card). func (ui *Context) ClipboardText() string ClipboardText is the text on the system's clipboard, "" when there is none. func (ui *Context) Column(content func()) Column stacks what content adds from top to bottom, across the whole width. func (ui *Context) Copy(text string) Copy puts a text on the system's clipboard (a link, a code, what a row holds), to paste in another application. func (ui *Context) Describe(description Description) Describe tells a screen reader more about the box added just before it (a control, a text): what it is, its name, its value and its state. func (ui *Context) DragSource(name string, payload any, layout Layout, content func()) bool DragSource adds a box whose content can be dragged away, carrying payload: press it and move the pointer a few pixels. func (ui *Context) Dragging() (Drag, bool) Dragging tells whether a payload is being dragged, and where the pointer is: a program shows where it would land on its scene while Drag.OverScreen is true. func (ui *Context) Drawing() *draw2d.List Drawing is the draw list the interface paints into; give it to the scene's overlay once (world.Overlay.Drawing = ui.Drawing()) and go-renderer draws it after every frame. func (ui *Context) DropTarget(name string, layout Layout, accepts func(payload any) bool, content func()) (payload any, dropped bool) DropTarget adds a box that takes dragged payloads. func (ui *Context) DroppedOnScreen() (Drag, bool) DroppedOnScreen tells, on the step the button is let go, whether a payload was dropped on the open screen, with the pointer's place: the program drops it on its scene there. func (ui *Context) EditTypedField(edit KeyboardText) EditTypedField puts what an on-screen keyboard made of the field's text in it, in the next frame: the field takes the whole text as typing (one line, cut at its MaxLength), the selection and the word being composed. func (ui *Context) EditingWords() EditingWords EditingWords are the labels the bar over a selection shows: the ones set, or English. func (ui *Context) End() End lays the interface out, paints it into the draw list and tells the input state whether the interface has the mouse or the keyboard. func (ui *Context) FieldFocused(name string) bool FieldFocused tells whether the text field of a name, in the same scope, has the keyboard: a program that draws the field's box itself (a Material field, with its text before and after) colours it by that. func (ui *Context) FlatButton(label string) bool FlatButton adds a button with no fill or border until hovered: menu bars and toolbars. func (ui *Context) FlatIconButton(icon, label string) bool FlatIconButton is FlatButton with an icon; with an empty label it is a square icon button. func (ui *Context) Focus(path ...string) Focus gives the keyboard to a text field or a number field, found by its scopes and label as Area finds it, with its whole text selected: to start typing in a search box on a shortcut, or in the first field of a form that just opened. func (ui *Context) FocusField(name string) FocusField gives the keyboard to the text field of a name, in the same scope, from the next time it is built: a search that opens ready to type in. func (ui *Context) Fold(name string, open bool, duration time.Duration, layout Layout, content func()) Fold lays content out in a box that opens to the content's height and closes to nothing with motion, clipping what does not show yet: the answer under a question, more under a list row. func (ui *Context) Frame(layout Layout, look Look, content func()) Frame adds a box with a layout and a look (fill, border, corners, shadow). func (ui *Context) Grid(columns int, content func()) Grid lays out what content adds in rows of a number of equal columns, across the whole width. func (ui *Context) HasKeyboard() bool HasKeyboard tells whether the interface reads Tab, Enter and Space in this frame. func (ui *Context) Heading(text string) Heading adds a line of bold, larger text: the title of a group. func (ui *Context) Icon(name string) Icon adds an icon (a Lucide name, https://lucide.dev ) at the theme's icon size. func (ui *Context) IconButton(icon, label string) bool IconButton adds a button with an icon (a Lucide name) before its label; with an empty label it is a square button with the icon alone, named by the icon. func (ui *Context) IconSized(name string, size float32, color draw2d.Color) IconSized adds an icon of a size and colour. func (ui *Context) Image(picture *draw2d.Image, layout Layout, radius float32) Image adds a picture filling a box laid out as any other (a photo in a card, a person's avatar): scaled to cover it and cropped evenly where their shapes differ, its corners rounded by radius. func (ui *Context) Insets() Insets Insets returns what the system draws over the window's edges. func (ui *Context) Label(text string) Label adds a line of body text. func (ui *Context) List(name string, layout Layout, count int, rowHeight float32, row func(index int)) List shows count rows of the same height in a scroll area and builds only the rows that can be seen, so a list of ten thousand rows costs what a list of twenty does. func (ui *Context) ListBox(name string, layout Layout, items []string, selected *int) bool ListBox shows items as a scrolling list of selectable rows and returns true when the selection changes. func (ui *Context) LongPressed() bool LongPressed tells whether the control added just before it was long-pressed in this frame: a finger held still on it for half a second, or the right mouse button pressed on it. func (ui *Context) MenuButton(icon, label string, content func()) MenuButton adds a flat button with an optional icon (a Lucide name); clicking it opens a menu under it, over everything, whose items content adds with MenuItem (and Separator between groups). func (ui *Context) MenuItem(icon, label, hint string) bool MenuItem adds an item to the menu being built: an optional icon, a label and an optional hint on the right (a keyboard shortcut, say). func (ui *Context) Modal(name string, options LayerOptions, content func()) (dismissed bool) Modal shows content over everything with what is behind it dimmed, as Sheet does, but drawn entirely by the program: a dialog, a sheet from the bottom of a phone. func (ui *Context) NumberField(name string, value *float32, minimum, maximum, step float32, format string) bool NumberField adds a number between minimum and maximum, shown with format (for example "%.0f nm"), with buttons to take a step off or add one. func (ui *Context) Overlay(name string, options LayerOptions, content func()) Overlay shows content over the screen and its panels without dimming or blocking what is behind it: a note at the bottom with an action in it, a floating toolbar. func (ui *Context) Paint(layout Layout, paint func(area draw2d.Rect, drawing *draw2d.List)) Paint adds a box laid out as any other, which the program paints itself once the layout knows where it is: a shape go-ui has no control for (a loading indicator, a wave, a chart). func (ui *Context) Panel(title string, content func()) Panel adds a floating panel with a title bar; drag the bar to move it, click the chevron to fold it. func (ui *Context) PanelWith(title string, options PanelOptions, content func()) PanelWith adds a panel placed and sized by options. func (ui *Context) Pointer() (x, y float32) Pointer is where the pointer is, in the window's layout pixels: a finger on a touch screen. func (ui *Context) Pop() Pop closes the scope opened last. func (ui *Context) Popover(name string, open *bool, look Look, content func()) Popover floats a box of the program's own under the control added just before it, over everything, at least as wide as the control: a dropdown's choices, a small form about a row. func (ui *Context) Pressing() bool Pressing tells whether the pointer is pressed now: a finger is on a touch screen, the mouse's left button is down. func (ui *Context) PrimaryButton(label string) bool PrimaryButton adds a button for the main action of a panel. func (ui *Context) PrimaryIconButton(icon, label string) bool PrimaryIconButton is PrimaryButton with an icon (a Lucide name) before its label: the main action of a panel, such as adding a new thing. func (ui *Context) Push(name string) Push opens a scope: ids of the controls added until Pop are made from this name too. func (ui *Context) ReleaseKeyboard() ReleaseKeyboard gives the keyboard back to the program and takes the focus off the controls. func (ui *Context) RemovableChip(icon, label string, look ChipLook) (clicked, removed bool) RemovableChip is a Chip with a small × after its label. func (ui *Context) RequestFrame(delay time.Duration) RequestFrame asks the window for another frame within a delay, even if no input arrives: for a program that animates something of its own (a clock, a replay). func (ui *Context) Resizable(name string, side Side, size *float32, minimum, maximum float32, layout Layout, content func()) bool Resizable adds a box whose width (with its handle on the right or left side) or height (bottom or top) the person changes by dragging its edge, between minimum and maximum pixels (0 = no maximum). func (ui *Context) Row(content func()) Row lines up what content adds from left to right, across the whole width, centred vertically. func (ui *Context) ScreenReaderAct(id ID, action ReaderAction) ScreenReaderAct does what a screen reader asks of a node, in the next frame: a press clicks the control as a tap would, so whatever the program does on a click happens. func (ui *Context) ScreenReaderNodes() []AccessibleNode ScreenReaderNodes is what the last frame showed, for a screen reader, in reading order: the window's own first, then what panels, sheets and popups hold, front-most last. func (ui *Context) ScreenReaderOn() bool ScreenReaderOn tells whether a screen reader is on (SetScreenReader). func (ui *Context) ScreenReaderSetText(id ID, text string) ScreenReaderSetText replaces a field's whole text with what a screen reader typed, pasted or dictated into it, in the next frame, without bringing the keyboard up. func (ui *Context) ScrollArea(name string, layout Layout, content func()) ScrollArea adds a box whose content scrolls up and down when it is taller than the box: with the wheel or the trackpad over it, by dragging the thin bar on its right, or, on a touch screen, by dragging the content with a finger, which glides on when let go. func (ui *Context) ScrollOffset(name string) float32 ScrollOffset tells how far a scroll area's content is scrolled from its top, as of the last frame: a bar over a list shrinks or takes a colour as the list goes up under it. func (ui *Context) ScrollPull(name string) (pulling, releasedAt float32) ScrollPull tells how far a finger is pulling a scroll area's content down past its top, and, in the frame the finger lets go, how far it was pulled then (zero otherwise): a list refreshes when pulled far enough and let go. func (ui *Context) Select(name string, selected *int, options []string) bool Select adds a field showing the selected option; clicking it opens the list of options over everything. func (ui *Context) Selectable(icon, label string, selected bool) bool Selectable adds an item with an optional icon that shows whether it is selected, and returns true on the step it is clicked. func (ui *Context) Separator() Separator draws a thin line across the row or column it is in. func (ui *Context) SetEditingWords(words EditingWords) SetEditingWords sets the labels of the bar over a selection, in the person's language. func (ui *Context) SetInsets(insets Insets) SetInsets tells the interface what the system draws over the window; the window calls it. func (ui *Context) SetScreenReader(on bool) SetScreenReader tells the interface whether a screen reader is on; the window does, on a phone. func (ui *Context) SetScreenReaderFocus(id ID) SetScreenReaderFocus says which node the screen reader is on (0 for none), so the interface rings it, as a phone rings what TalkBack reads. func (ui *Context) SetTextScale(scale float32) SetTextScale sets how much larger than its size each text is drawn: the person's text size, as a phone's settings give it (1.3 for a larger text). func (ui *Context) Sheet(title string, options SheetOptions, content func()) (dismissed bool) Sheet shows a card in the middle of the window, over everything, with what is behind it dimmed: a question to confirm, a short form. func (ui *Context) Size() (width, height float32) Size returns the window's size in this frame, in layout pixels: a program chooses a layout by it (a list alone on a phone, a list and its details side by side on a tablet). func (ui *Context) Slider(name string, value *float32, minimum, maximum float32) bool Slider adds a track with a knob to drag between minimum and maximum, across the width it is given. func (ui *Context) SliderStep(name string, value *float32, minimum, maximum, step float32) bool SliderStep is Slider with the value kept to whole steps (0 = any value). func (ui *Context) Spacer() Spacer takes the free space of the row or column it is in, pushing what follows to the end. func (ui *Context) SwipeBox(name string, layout Layout, axis Direction, content func(swipe Swipe)) SwipeBox lays content out in a box a finger drags along an axis (sideways, for pages, cards in a row, a row swiped away): content is given what the finger does in this frame, and places itself by it. func (ui *Context) Table(name string, layout Layout, columns []Column, rows func(table *Table)) Table adds a table with a header and rows that scroll under it: rows adds the rows, with table.Row, and table.Group for a caption between groups of rows. func (ui *Context) Tabs(name string, selected *int, labels ...string) bool Tabs adds a row of segments, one per label, with the selected one raised; clicking a segment selects it. func (ui *Context) TakeKeyboard() TakeKeyboard gives the interface the keyboard, as a game does when it opens its own menu: Tab then moves between the controls until Escape or ReleaseKeyboard gives the keys back. func (ui *Context) Text(text string, style TextStyle) Text adds a line

reference/window.title: window
reference/window.text: window import "github.com/akrck02/go-ui/window" Package window runs an application that is only an interface: a window with no 3D scene, where go-ui draws everything on the theme's background, in one draw call. On the desktop it opens the window through go-renderer (so it needs cgo, and Metal or OpenGL 4.1); built for WebAssembly (GOOS=js) the window is a canvas in a web page, drawn through WebGL2; built for Android (with gomobile) it is the application's activity, drawn through OpenGL ES. The window draws only when something happens: input, a resize, a frame a control asks for (a caret's blink, a tooltip due) or Wake. In between the program sleeps and uses no processor, which a laptop's or a phone's battery needs from an application that is mostly still. Set Options.Continuous for one that animates all the time. window.Run(window.Options{Title: "Lighthouses", Width: 1280, Height: 800}, func(context *ui.Context) { context.Label("Hello") }) Functions Function func AskForNotifications() AskForNotifications asks the person to allow notifications; on the desktop there is nothing to ask. func FeelLongPress() FeelLongPress gives the buzz of a long press on a phone; a desktop has nothing to buzz. func ForgetPreference(name string) error ForgetPreference lets go of the value kept under a name. func Graphics() string Graphics describes a phone's OpenGL ES and GPU; on the desktop it is "". func KeepPreference(name, value string) error KeepPreference keeps a value under a name, replacing the one there was. func LastCrash() string LastCrash returns the report of the last run's crash; on the desktop the terminal shows it, and this is always "". func NotificationsAllowed() bool NotificationsAllowed tells whether the program may show notifications: not yet on the desktop. func Notify(id int, title, text string) bool Notify shows a notification; on the desktop it does not yet, and returns false. func OpenLink(link string) bool OpenLink opens a link in the application that shows it (the browser for a web page), through the computer's own command for that. func Preference(name string) (string, bool) Preference is the value kept under a name, and whether there is one. func Run(options Options, build func(context *ui.Context)) error Run opens the window and calls build in every update step, between the interface's Begin and End, until the window is closed. func RunWith(context *ui.Context, options Options, build func(context *ui.Context)) error RunWith is Run with an interface context of your own (a custom theme or measurer). func Share(title, text string) bool Share offers a text to other applications; a desktop has no sheet for that, so it returns false (put the text on the clipboard instead). func SystemPrefersDark() bool SystemPrefersDark tells whether the system is set to a dark theme. func Wake() Wake makes the window draw a frame now: call it when the program's data changes on another goroutine (a file loaded, a message arrived), since the window otherwise sleeps until input. Constants and variables var ErrVideoUnsupported = errors.New("window: films do not play here yet") ErrVideoUnsupported is OpenVideo's answer where films do not play yet. var PaletteTones = [13]int{0, 10, 50, 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 900, 1000} PaletteTones are the shades' numbers in Android's names, in the order of each palette: 0 is white, 500 the middle, 1000 black. Backend Backend is the graphics interface a window draws through. type Backend string const ( Automatic Backend = "" // Metal on macOS, falling back to OpenGL if it cannot start; OpenGL elsewhere Metal Backend = "metal" // only on macOS OpenGL Backend = "opengl" // OpenGL 4.1, on every desktop system ) Function or method func (backend *Backend) Set(text string) error Set reads a backend from a flag: automatic, metal or opengl. func (backend *Backend) String() string Options Options configure the window. type Options struct { Title string Width, Height int // window size in window pixels; 0 = 1280 × 800 // MinWidth and MinHeight stop the window from being made smaller than the layout needs; 0 = no // limit. MinWidth, MinHeight int CapturePath string // draw one frame to this PNG (hidden window) and return, for documentation and tests NoVsync bool // draw as fast as possible instead of waiting for the display Dark bool // start with the dark theme // Continuous draws every frame, at the display's rate, instead of only when something // happens: for an interface that animates all the time. It uses far more battery. Continuous bool // Backend is what draws the window: Automatic (Metal on macOS, OpenGL elsewhere), Metal or // OpenGL. In a web page it is always WebGL2. Backend Backend // Canvas is the id of the page's canvas to draw in, in a web page; empty = the first canvas. // The window is the canvas: Width, Height and Title follow the page. Canvas string // Scene, when set, puts a 3D scene behind the interface. It is called at every step after the // interface, with the input the interface did not claim (so the program can turn its camera // without fighting a slider), and returns what to show this frame: nil for no scene. On the // desktop a window with a scene draws through OpenGL. Scene func(state *input.State, step float64) *SceneView // MaxFramesPerSecond caps how often the window draws, to spare a battery; 0 = 60 on a phone, // the display's own rate elsewhere (where vsync keeps it). MaxFramesPerSecond int // Hidden is called when the program leaves the screen: on a phone, another application comes // up or the phone locks, and the system may end the program after that without a word; in a // browser, the page is hidden; on the desktop, the window closes. Keep what must survive then // (KeepPreference). It runs on the goroutine that builds the interface, except in a browser. Hidden func() // Shown is called when the program comes back on the screen after Hidden: on a phone, back from // another application or the lock screen (and at its start); in a browser, when the page shows // again. It is the moment to play again what Hidden stopped, such as a sound. On the desktop, // where a hidden window has closed, it is not called. Shown func() } Function or method func (options *Options) RegisterFlags(flags *flag.FlagSet) RegisterFlags declares -width, -height, -capture, -no-vsync, -dark, -continuous and -backend. Palettes Palettes are the colours a phone made from its wallpaper (Android 12 and later, Material You): three accent palettes and two neutral ones, each in thirteen shades from white to black, as Android names them (system_accent1_0 … system_accent1_1000). A program that builds its colours from them matches the phone, as the system's own applications do. type Palettes struct { Accent1, Accent2, Accent3, Neutral1, Neutral2 [13]draw2d.Color } Function or method func SystemPalettes() (Palettes, bool) SystemPalettes returns the colours a phone made from its wallpaper; a desktop has none. SceneView SceneView is a 3D scene seen from a camera, drawn behind the interface. type SceneView struct { World *scene.Scene Camera models.Camera } Video Video plays a film's pictures (not yet its sound) in a draw2d.Image the program draws, with ui.Context.Image or any piece that shows a picture. A program opens it once, calls Update in every frame it is shown, and plays, pauses or loops it. On Android the phone's own decoders read MP4 and WebM films (H.264, H.265, VP8, VP9, AV1); in a browser, those the browser plays; on the desktop, films do not play yet (OpenVideo says so). type Video struct { Loop bool // start again at the end // Has unexported fields. } Function or method func OpenVideo(film []byte) (*Video, error) OpenVideo opens a film (the bytes of an MP4 or WebM file, often embedded in the program), paused at its start. func (video *Video) Close() Close lets go of the film's decoder. func (video *Video) Duration() time.Duration Duration is how long the film lasts; 0 until known. func (video *Video) Ended() bool Ended tells whether the film reached its end (and does not loop). func (video *Video) Pause() Pause stops the film where it is. func (video *Video) Picture() *draw2d.Image Picture is the film's current picture, to draw; nil until the film's size is known. func (video *Video) Play() Play plays the film from where it is; at its end, from its start. func (video *Video) Playing() bool Playing tells whether the film is playing. func (video *Video) Position() time.Duration Position is how far into the film it is. func (video *Video) Update(context *ui.Context) Update brings the picture to the film's position, and asks for the next frame while it plays. ← Reference · generated from the doc comments by generate.py

the-quest/controls-and-forms.title: Lesson 3: controls and forms
the-quest/controls-and-forms.text: Lesson 3: controls and forms In this lesson the list becomes something you choose from, and the content a form that edits the lighthouse chosen: its name, colour, range, period, whether it is lit and whether it has a foghorn. Mission Pieces Time A form that edits the lighthouse chosen Selectable , text and number fields, selects, sliders 15 min The idea Each control is a window onto one of your variables : the field shows light.name and, when you type, writes into it. The list, the heading and the status bar look through their own windows at the same variable, so they always agree. The form of North Point: a name field, a colour select, a range with − and +, a period slider, a switch and a checkbox Choosing from a list Selectable(icon, label, selected) is a row that shows whether it is chosen and returns true when clicked. In a loop, each row needs an id of its own: two lighthouses could share a name, so each row opens a scope with its index. // sideList lists the lighthouses that match the search; a click selects one. Its right edge can // be dragged to make it wider. func (program *register) sideList(context *ui.Context) { column := ui.Layout{Direction: ui.Vertical, Height: ui.Grow(), Padding: ui.Pad(8), Gap: 2} context.Resizable("side", ui.RightSide, &program.sideWidth, 180, 400, column, func() { for index, light := range program.lighthouses { if !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(light.name), strings.ToLower(program.search)) { continue } context.Push(fmt.Sprint(index)) // two lighthouses may share a name: give each row its own id icon := "lightbulb-off" if light.lit { icon = "lightbulb" } if context.Selectable(icon, light.name, index == program.selected) { program.selected = index } context.Pop() } }) } The search box goes in the toolbar, after the Spacer . A text field edits your string in place and returns true on the frames it changes; here the list simply reads program.search at the next frame: context.TextFieldWith("search", &program.search, ui.TextFieldOptions{Placeholder: "Search", Width: ui.Fixed(200)}) The search "ea" leaves East Cape alone in the list For thousands of rows, List(name, layout, count, rowHeight, row) builds only the rows in sight, and Table adds a header, columns and groups ( the guide ). The form Each control takes a pointer to the value it edits, and returns true when the person changed it. A small helper lines the labels up in a column of their own: // field is a row of the form: a label in a column of its own width, then the control. func field(context *ui.Context, label string, control func()) { context.Row(func() { context.Box(ui.Layout{Width: ui.Fixed(80)}, func() { context.Label(label) }) control() }) } // details is the form of the lighthouse selected. func (program *register) details(context *ui.Context) { area := ui.Layout{Direction: ui.Vertical, Width: ui.Grow(), Height: ui.Grow(), Padding: ui.Pad(24), Gap: 12} context.Box(area, func() { if program.selected < 0 { context.Caption("Choose a lighthouse on the left, or add one.") return } light := &program.lighthouses[program.selected] context.Row(func() { context.Heading(light.name) context.Spacer() favouriteButton(context, &light.favourite) // lesson 5 }) field(context, "Name", func() { context.TextFieldWith("name", &light.name, ui.TextFieldOptions{MaxLength: 40}) }) field(context, "Colour", func() { context.Select("colour", &light.colour, colours) }) field(context, "Range", func() { context.NumberField("range", &light.rangeNM, 1, 30, 0.5, "%.1f nm") }) field(context, "Period", func() { context.SliderStep("period", &light.period, 1, 20, 1) context.Caption(fmt.Sprintf("%.0f s", light.period)) }) context.Toggle("Lit", &light.lit) context.Checkbox("Foghorn", &light.foghorn) context.Spacer() context.Row(func() { context.Spacer() if context.Button("Remove") { program.removing = true // lesson 4 asks first } }) }) } Until lesson 5, leave out the favouriteButton line. Notice what is not there: no "on change" handler copies the name into the list. The field writes light.name , and the list, the heading and the status bar read it at the next frame. The controls you used Control Edits Feels like TextField(name, &text) , TextFieldWith(…, options) A string Selection, the clipboard, undo, Tab to the next field; Placeholder , MaxLength , Secret Select(name, &index, options) An int A field that opens its list over everything; arrows and Enter work NumberField(name, &value, minimum, maximum, step, format) A float32 − and +, drag sideways, or click and type Slider(name, &value, minimum, maximum) , SliderStep(…, step) A float32 Click to jump, drag, Shift for fine steps Toggle(label, &on) A bool A settings row with a switch Checkbox(label, &on) A bool A box to tick Tabs(name, &index, labels…) An int A segmented row; show the tab's content with an if ListBox(name, layout, items, &index) An int A scrolling list of selectable items The full list, with buttons, chips, images and tooltips, is in the reference . 📝 The keyboard and the 3D view. While a field has the keyboard, Go UI claims it, so a 3D view's shortcuts do not take the letters you type ( lesson 6 ). Checkpoint Click East Cape : the form shows its name, colour, range and period; rename it and the list changes as you type; ea in the search leaves it alone in the list. Achievement unlocked: Clerk What you learnt Selectable rows in a loop, each in a scope of its own ( Push , Pop ). Controls edit the value they point to and return true when it changed. Every part of the screen reads the same data at every frame, so nothing needs syncing. Bonus (optional) Show a warning under the range when it is above 25 nm, in the theme's warning colour. ← Lesson 2 · Lesson 4: menus, sheets and notes →

the-quest/controls-of-your-own.title: Lesson 5: controls of your own
the-quest/controls-of-your-own.text: Lesson 5: controls of your own Go UI's controls are built from the same pieces you can use. In this lesson you make a favourite star from a clickable box, tell screen readers what it is, paint a strip of your own, and give the register a theme colour of its own. Mission Pieces Time A favourite star, and a theme of your own Clickable , Describe , Paint , Theme 20 min The idea Go UI's own buttons are made of the same bricks you can use: a box that reacts to the pointer, with a look for each state. And the theme is a paint chart : change one swatch and every wall painted with it changes. The finished register in the dark theme, North Point a favourite, its light's character painted under the period A clickable box Clickable(name, layout, looks, content) is any box that reacts to the pointer: it is painted with one of three Look s (left alone, hovered, pressed) and returns true when clicked. Inside, put anything. Go UI's own buttons are made this way. // favouriteButton is a control of the program's own: a star, golden while the lighthouse is a // favourite. A click flips it. func favouriteButton(context *ui.Context, favourite *bool) { theme := context.Theme square := ui.Layout{Width: ui.Fixed(36), Height: ui.Fixed(36), AlignX: ui.Center, AlignY: ui.Center} looks := ui.Looks{ Hovered: ui.Look{Fill: theme.Sunken, Radius: 18}, Pressed: ui.Look{Fill: theme.Line, Radius: 18}, } colour := theme.InkQuiet if *favourite { colour = draw2d.Hex("#e8a317") } if context.Clickable("favourite", square, looks, func() { context.IconSized("star", 20, colour) }) { *favourite = !*favourite } // a screen reader would only hear "star": say what it is and whether it is on context.Describe(ui.Description{Role: ui.SwitchRole, Label: "Favourite", Checked: *favourite}) } It goes in the heading row of the form, after a Spacer (lesson 3 already calls it). Screen readers A screen reader (TalkBack on Android) speaks what is on the screen for someone who cannot see it. Go UI works out what to say from the boxes: a button reads its text, a checkbox says whether it is ticked. A box of your own holds only an icon, which would be read as "star". Describe , right after the control, says what it really is: ui.Description field Says Role What kind of thing: ButtonRole , SwitchRole , CheckboxRole , SliderRole , FieldRole … Label Its name Value What it holds Checked , Selected , Disabled Its state Hidden Leave it out: a decoration It costs nothing while no screen reader is on. The guide explains how the screen is read. Painting your own shapes When no control draws what you need, Paint(layout, paint) adds a box that is laid out like any other and then handed to your function, with its final rectangle and Go Renderer's draw2d.List to draw into: rounded rectangles, shadows, text, icons, pictures. The register shows a light's character , a mark for every flash in twenty seconds: // flashes paints the light's character over twenty seconds: a mark for every flash. func flashes(context *ui.Context, period float32, colour draw2d.Color) { theme := context.Theme context.Paint(ui.Layout{Width: ui.Grow(), Height: ui.Fixed(24)}, func(area draw2d.Rect, drawing *draw2d.List) { drawing.Rectangle(area, 4, theme.Sunken, draw2d.Transparent, 0) const seconds = 20 for second := float32(0); second < seconds; second += period { x := area.X + area.Width*second/seconds drawing.Rectangle(draw2d.Rect{X: x + 2, Y: area.Y + 4, Width: 6, Height: area.Height - 8}, 3, colour, draw2d.Transparent, 0) } }) } // lampColours are the colours a flash is painted in, by colours' order. var lampColours = []draw2d.Color{draw2d.Hex("#f5f0d0"), draw2d.Hex("#d64545"), draw2d.Hex("#3f9b5b"), draw2d.Hex("#e8a317")} field(context, "Character", func() { flashes(context, light.period, lampColours[light.colour]) }) Coordinates are layout pixels from the window's top-left corner, like everything in Go UI. Themes Every control reads its colours and sizes from context.Theme : surfaces, inks, lines, the primary colour, text sizes, the height of a control, gaps, padding and corner radii. ui.LightTheme() is the default and ui.DarkTheme() its dark twin ( -dark , or window.SystemPrefersDark() ). Change a token and every control follows: func (program *register) build(context *ui.Context) { context.Theme.Primary = draw2d.Hex("#00796b") // a teal of the register's own context.Theme.PrimaryTint = context.Theme.Primary.WithAlpha(0.12) … The register in its own teal Token Used for Background , Surface , Sunken Behind everything; panels and bars; wells and hovered controls Ink , InkSoft , InkQuiet Body text; secondary text and icons; hints Line , ControlLine Separators; the borders of fields and buttons Primary , OnPrimary , PrimaryTint The main action, the text on it, a light wash of it Positive , Warning , Danger States TextSize , HeadingSize , ControlHeight , Gap , Padding , ControlRadius … Sizes, in layout pixels Moving things Controls of your own can move. context.Animate(name, target, duration) eases a value towards a target and asks for frames only while it moves; context.Appear(name, duration) eases from 0 to 1 the first time something is shown; context.Fold(name, open, duration, layout, content) opens a box to its content's height and closes it to nothing. Checkpoint A star beside the name turns gold when clicked; under the period, a strip shows a mark for every flash; everything primary is teal. Achievement unlocked: Craftsman What you learnt Clickable makes any box a control, with a look for each state. Describe tells screen readers what a control of your own is. Paint draws your own shapes in a laid-out box; the theme's tokens colour and size everything. Bonus (optional) Make the star grow a little while the pointer is over it, easing between the two sizes. The whole program main.go : // Command register is the go-ui tutorial's program: a register of lighthouses, with a list to // choose one, a form to edit it, a search, a menu to add one and a sheet that asks before removing. package main import ( "flag" "fmt" "github.com/akrck02/go-renderer/draw2d" "log" "strings" ui "github.com/akrck02/go-ui" "github.com/akrck02/go-ui/window" ) // lighthouse is the program's own data: the interface shows it and changes it, and keeps none. type lighthouse struct { name string colour int // an index into colours rangeNM float32 // how far the light is seen, in nautical miles period float32 // seconds between flashes lit bool foghorn bool favourite bool } var colours = []string{"White", "Red", "Green", "Amber"} // register is everything the program remembers between frames. type register struct { lighthouses []lighthouse selected int // -1 = none search string sideWidth float32 removing bool // the sheet asking before a removal is open added int // how many were added, to name new ones } func main() { options := window.Options{Title: "Lighthouse register"} options.RegisterFlags(flag.CommandLine) flag.Parse() options.MinWidth, options.MinHeight = 640, 400 // the smallest the layout still works at program := &register{ lighthouses: []lighthouse{ {name: "North Point", rangeNM: 18, period: 5, lit: true}, {name: "East Cape", colour: 1, rangeNM: 12, period: 3, lit: true, foghorn: true}, {name: "Harbour Mole", colour: 2, rangeNM: 6, period: 2}, {name: "South Reef", colour: 3, rangeNM: 15, period: 10, lit: true}, }, sideWidth: 240, } if err := window.Run(options, program.build); err != nil { log.Fatal(err) } } // build describes the whole interface, in every frame. func (program *register) build(context *ui.Context) { context.Theme.Primary = draw2d.Hex("#00796b") // a teal of the register's own context.Theme.PrimaryTint = context.Theme.Primary.WithAlpha(0.12) context.Box(ui.Layout{Direction: ui.Vertical, Width: ui.Grow(), Height: ui.Grow()}, func() { program.toolbar(context) context.Box(ui.Layout{Width: ui.Grow(), Height: ui.Grow()}, func() { program.sideList(context) program.details(context) }) program.statusBar(context) }) program.confirmRemoval(context) } // toolbar is the bar across the top: the title, a search box and a menu to add a lighthouse. func (program *register) toolbar(context *ui.Context) { theme := context.Theme bar := ui.Layout{Width: ui.Grow(), Padding: ui.PadXY(16, 8), Gap: 8, AlignY: ui.Center} context.Frame(bar, ui.Look{Fill: theme.Surface}, func() { context.Icon("lighthouse") context.Heading("Lighthouses") context.Spacer() context.TextFieldWith("search", &program.search, ui.TextFieldOptions{Placeholder: "Search", Width: ui.Fixed(200)}) context.MenuButton("plus", "Add", func() { if context.MenuItem("lighthouse", "Lighthouse", "") { program.add() } if context.MenuItem("copy", "Copy of the selected one", "") && program.selected >= 0 { program.lighthouses = append(program.lighthouses, program.lighthouses[program.selected]) program.selected = len(program.lighthouses) - 1 } }) }) context.Separator() } // sideList lists the lighthouses that match the search; a click selects one. Its right edge can // be dragged to make it wider. func (program *register) sideList(context *ui.Context) { column := ui.Layout{Direction: ui.Vertical, Height: ui.Grow(), Padding: ui.Pad(8), Gap: 2} context.Resizable("side", ui.RightSide, &program.sideWidth, 180, 400, column, func() { for index, light := range program.lighthouses { if !strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(light.name), strings.ToLower(program.search)) { continue } context.Push(fmt.Sprint(index)) // two lighthouses may share a name: give each row its own id icon := "lightbulb-off" if light.lit { icon = "lightbulb" } if context.Selectable(icon, light.name, index == program.selected) { program.selected = index } context.Pop() } }) } // details is the form of the lighthouse selected. func (program *register) details(context *ui.Context) { area := ui.Layout{Direction: ui.Vertical, Width: ui.Grow(), Height: ui.Grow(), Padding: ui.Pad(24), Gap: 12} context.Box(area, func() { if program.selected < 0 { context.Caption("Choose a lighthouse on the left, or add one.") return } light := &program.lighthouses[program.selected] context.Row(func() { context.Heading(light.name) context.Spacer() favouriteButton(context, &light.favourite) }) field(context, "Name", func() { context.TextFieldWith("name", &light.name, ui.TextFieldOptions{MaxLength: 40}) }) field(context, "Colour", func() { context.Select("colour", &light.colour, colours) }) field(context, "Range", func() { context.NumberField("range", &light.rangeNM, 1, 30, 0.5, "%.1f nm") }) field(context, "Period", func() { context.SliderStep("period", &light.period, 1, 20, 1) context.Caption(fmt.Sprintf("%.0f s", light.period)) }) field(context, "Character", func() { flashes(context, light.period, lampColours[light.colour]) }) context.Toggle("Lit", &light.lit) context.Checkbox("Foghorn", &light.foghorn) context.Spacer() context.Row(func() { context.Spacer() if context.Button("Remove") { program.removing = true } }) }) } // field is a row of the form: a label in a column of its own width, then the control. func field(context *ui.Context, label string, control func()) { context.Row(func() { context.Box(ui.Layout{Width: ui.Fixed(80)}, func() { context.Label(label) }) control() }) } // statusBar sums the register up at the foot of the window. func (program *register) statusBar(context *ui.Context) { lit := 0 for _, light := range program.lighthouses { if light.lit { lit++ } } context.Separator() context.Frame(ui.Layout{Width: ui.Grow(), Padding: ui.PadXY(16, 6)}, ui.Look{Fill: context.Theme.Surface}, func() { context.Caption(fmt.Sprintf("%d lighthouses, %d lit", len(program.lighthouses), lit)) }) } // confirmRemoval asks before a lighthouse is taken out of the register. func (program *register) confirmRemoval(context *ui.Context) { if !program.removing { return } name := program.lighthouses[program.selected].name dismissed := context.Sheet("Remove lighthouse", ui.SheetOptions{}, func() { context.Label(fmt.Sprintf("Take %s out of the register?", name)) context.Row(func() { context.Spacer() if context.Button("Keep it") { program.removing = false } if context.PrimaryButton("Remove") { program.remove() context.Toast(name+" was removed", false) } }) }) if dismissed { program.removing = false } } func (program *register) add() { program.added++ program.lighthouses = append(program.lighthouses, lighthouse{name: fmt.Sprintf("New lighthouse %d", program.added), rangeNM: 10, period: 5}) program.selected = len(program.lighthouses) - 1 program.search = "" } func (program *register) remove() { program.lighthouses = append(program.lighthouses[:program.selected], program.lighthouses[program.selected+1:]...) program.selected = min(program.selected, len(program.lighthouses)-1) program.removing = false } favourite.go and flashes.go are above, each with package main and its imports ( github.com/akrck02/go-renderer/draw2d and ui "github.com/akrck02/go-ui" ). ← Lesson 4 · Lesson 6: over a 3D scene →
